notes.title: Behind the symphony #5: Q&A The Lore of Symphonia
notes.notes:
Musical greetings, friends and virtuosos ! 

In today’s making-of, we’re tackling some lore questions submitted by the community of players on our Discord server (link in the store page !). 
Thanks again for your submissions and let’s start !

---

Q : Can we get a short introduction to Philemon's fellow founders (i.e. their names, instruments, and relations [I headcannon them to be siblings])?

A : Philemon founded the realm together with three fellow musicians, and each of them was a virtuoso, playing on a different family of instruments (Strings, Percussions, Brass, Woodwinds). Their names and other characteristics have yet to be revealed, however, we know that they were playing together as an orchestra in their native realm. They were eventually expelled and had to wander around until they founded Symphonia.

Q : What's with the founder's vanishing? Did something happen to them or did they go willingly?

A : As mentioned in the opening sequence, the founders disappeared when “something happened". We didn’t want to deliver that information in Symphonia, because it is not a key information for the main narrative. However, I can say that they didn’t leave willingly, and they are not just living somewhere else : they actually did vanish from the world, and it comes from a catastrophe that they triggered themselves. I am hoping I can say more about that in future works !

Q : What are the circumstances of the Heart stopping? Is it directly related to the vanishing? Was it sabotaged? Did it literally just stop one day?

A : The Heart is powered by musicians, and its function is to amplify music and direct it to all areas of the realm at the same time. The music as a lifeforce, allows the realm to prosper and the automatons to keep functionning. Knowing that, the explanation is simple : after the founders vanished, the prodigies tried to work together as a new orchestra, but couldn’t find a way to work together, and parted ways. Left without an orchestra, and feeding on the resentment of the prodigies, the Heart started to decay.

Q : Can we get names for the new orchestra's members? Or are epithets all they have?

A : As you might have noticed, the prodigies in Symphonia are automatons, created long ago by the founders. They don’t actually have birthnames so, feel free to give them some if you wish !

Q : Are there like confirmed ages or an age range for the NPCs and Philemon?

A : The vanishing of the founders occurred a very long time ago, at least several decades, and it is safe to assume that the foundation of Symphonia was closer in time to the vanishing than to the events played in the game. We can safely say that the founders were grown adults when they vanished, and had not lived longer than typical humans. The prodigies, as automatons, lived even longer than them, since they are still around. When the events of the game start, the realm has spent more time in decay than in prosperity.

Q : What happened to the area representing percussion?

A : It is hinted in the game that there is an area dedicated to percussion, as Philemon takes the place of the percussion prodigy during the last concert. However the Bandmaster does not mention the percussion prodigy when meeting Philemon. That’s because the area has become inaccessible and the prodigy is thought to be lost. We initially wanted to include this area in the game, but we couldn't find a way, for production reasons. Maybe they will come back at some point if the opportunity rises ?

Q : How come the Trickster is the only one without any robot subjects? Did the plants kill them or did they just get run out because of the plants?

A : We planned to have animal automatons in the Woodwinds Glasshouse, they are just kind of hidden from the player unfortunately, as we didn’t have enough time to create and integrate them. It is canon that the Trickster is the only “human” automaton in the area, though, as his solitude plays a big part in his character development.

---

And that is all for today ! To finish with, I’d like to thank again everyone who delved deep into the world of Symphonia, whether it is here on Steam, or on other platforms and consoles !
Oh, and do not hesitate to have a look on gamefairy.io, as we’re preparing an exclusive, limited edition for Symphonia on a famous red and blue console… 

Take care and see you in the next article ! =)

Sunny Peak 🌄

notes.title: Symphonia 1.1.2 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
[u][b]Symphonia 1.1.2 Patch Notes[/b][/u]

Hello everyone!

This update will be fairly short. We've mainly fixed bugs that could hinder the game experience, while waiting for a new update for minor level design balancing. Some bugs may persist, while others are still in the process of being fixed.

[u][b]Bugs : [/b][/u]

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug that can briefly lock the player into its bounce on a string animation
[*] Fixed a bug that prevented the respawn sound to play in certain conditions
[*] Fixed a bug that prevented the room transitions to occur in some rooms (in Brass and Woodwinds)
[*] Added safety measures to avoid a rare bug where Philemon gets stuck in its playing the violin state
[*] Fixed a bug that allowed Philemon to go under a horizontal string with the grappling bow
[*] Fixed a bug that prevented the Kinglet to appear in the machine at the end of the Brass Palace
[*] Fixed various sound issues around concerts and post concerts
[*] Fixed minor visual issues in the backgrounds in the Introduction area
[/list]

We'd like to thank the GDQ Hotfix for the partnership we had with them last month. The runs shown were impressive and it gives us great pleasure as developers to see people pushing the game to its limits! If you can to catch it up, you can go on the GDQ Youtube channel.

If some bugs are persistent you can always report them in our Discord server. Thanks again for your feedback and for playing the game. See you for the next patch!

Musically yours,
Sunny Peak 🌄

notes.title: Symphonia 1.1.0 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
Hello dear platforming lovers ! 

Today sees the launch of our first patch since launch day… It is a pretty big one, as we tried to tackle some of the most important problems we have been seeing in this first week : confusions about some features, and some annoyingly common bugs. Thanks again to the Symphonia Discord members for sending us your bugs, that really helps fixing them faster !

Without waiting, here are the patch notes for Symphonia 1.1.0 (spoilers ahead !) : 

Features : 

- Reworked the settings menu to clarify the utility of gameplay variants.
- Added a new warning popup, that appears if you enter secret areas without having the core abilities needed to complete the area.
- Added a new achievement, related to aura shards !
- Added a new splash screen (Razer Interhaptics).
- Changed the credits to include new entries for Razer Interhaptics.
- Removed the debug input for the camera movements.

Bugs : 

- Fixed a bug on the horizontal strings that allowed you to clip under when using the double jump on them.
- Fixed a bug that changed Philemon’s orientation when he died and stuck on a cushion at the same time.
- Fixed a bug that froze Philemon when using the grappling bow on a horizontal string.
- Fixed a bug that caused coins to instantly teleport if you died while collecting them.
- Fixed a bug that displayed unwanted dust vfx when the player tried to move during one of the Trickster’s cutscenes.
- Fixed a bug that caused Philemon to be unable to use the Wayfarer Tune in the Palace Jail.
- Fixed a bug that made the catapult preview and grappling bow trail go behind the scenery sometimes.
- Fixed a bug that caused some animation issues when using alt+tab at specific moments.
- Fixed a bug that caused Philemon’s animation to be wrong when launching the cutscene in the second room of Palace Jail.
- Fixed a bug that lowered the audio volume when dying while playing the Wayfarer Tune.
- Attempt to fix the bug that causes some rooms to not load sometimes.
- Fixed minor issues in audio.
- Fixed minor animation issues.
- Fixed many other tiny bugs and imprecise behaviors.

Thanks again for this awesome launch week and see you next week for another patch !

Musically yours,
Sunny Peak 🌄

notes.title: 🐍 Symphonia supports Razer's Sensa HD Haptics and Chroma peripherals!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44506357/2dfb5144b824da42307cfc0e957fced29fa2ef9d.jpg[/img]

Greetings all!

During the launch of [b]Symphonia[/b] last week, we have omitted to mention one piece of information. But perhaps you have already 'felt' it since it's a really tangible piece of information in the truest sense of the word.

If you've been following [b]Symphonia[/b] on Steam for a while (since around mid-September or earlier), you may have noticed that we announced at the time that [b]Symphonia[/b] would be one of the first titles to support Razer's [b]Sensa HD Haptics[/b] peripherals. You know, that gaming cushion that attaches to your chair and can literally kick your butt.

[b]And yes, we kept our word.[/b]

But let's start from the beginning, with two questions: [i]'Why are you doing this?'[/i] and [i]'How should a cushion for my chair improve my gaming experience?'[/i]. Let me answer the first question first: The reason is me, Tim. Hi! Well, personally I am very open-minded about such technical gadgets. And I am convinced that an intensive gaming experience can benefit from being more than just an audiovisual experience. I am a big fan of strengthening the immersion of video games to delve even deeper and making it possible to experience them with as many senses as possible.

That's exactly why I'm the one here at Headup who initiates such implementations. And so I asked myself which of our games could benefit from also being a 'tangible' experience (which is also the answer to the second question).

A platformer should do the trick, right? After all, it is a game in which you are jumping and bouncing around a lot, catapult yourself, glide through winds, slide down walls, miss jumps and landings, and much much more. And all these actions and movements in [b]Symphonia[/b] are accompanied and reinforced by haptic feedback.

The gaming cushion ([url=https://www.razer.com/gaming-chairs-accessories/razer-freyja]Razer Freyja[/url]) has six haptic zones: two in the shoulder blade area, two in the lower back area; one each on the left and on the right. Plus one zone under each bun. The haptic feedback can be controlled in terms of intensity and can therefore be adapted to different jumps by Philemon, for example. If he performs a simple jump, the bun zones vibrate slightly; but if he bounces or catapults himself with the bow of the violin, the vibration gets stronger.

We also play with the left and right zones of the gaming cushion: if you jump up between two walls in ping-pong style with a wall jump, the respective left and right jump is supported by the corresponding haptic feedback zone. And that feels really cool!

As I said, I am a friend of gimmicks that increase immersion. That's why I also love it when the gameplay is extended beyond the limits of the screen through RGB illumination. And that is the reason why the haptic effects are additionally supported by RGB effects in Razer's [b]Chroma[/b] ecosystem. A mistimed jump or an aimless landing is not only noticeable (you'll definitely get your butt kicked for dying!), but is also communicated by a red flash on the Chroma peripherals.

Well, in the end I can only speak for us (Headup and Sunny Peak) and myself personally, and we are really happy with the results of both [b]Sensa HD Haptics[/b] and [b]Chroma[/b] and how it supports and accompanies the [b]Symphonia[/b] experience and immersion.

Personally, I love it. ❤️ If I didn't already have it, the cushion would definitely be on top of my Christmas wish list.

Pre-seasonal greetings!
Tim

notes.title: 🎻 Behind the Symphony #4: What awaits you in Symphonia
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44506357/d82ac5e1c79981129de26c13425f383a579c2907.jpg[/img]

Hello again, dear musical friends! 

The release of [b]Symphonia[/b] is just around the corner now … the 5th of December is in just a few days! We thought we would take a bit of time to put together a summary of what you can expect in this game we’ve been building for many years now.

We are confident that you will enjoy your time with Philemon in this vibrant and colorful world, but we would rather avoid any confusion so you know exactly what kind of game you will get if you consider a stay in [b]Symphonia[/b]!

[b]So, that's what awaits you with Symphonia:[/b]

[list][*] A single-player, mostly linear 2D precision platformer, with a tight and aerial, non-violent gameplay, where your only enemies are the obstacles blocking your path forward.
[*] Progress through a multifaceted world by bouncing around, catapulting yourself to avoid obstacles and play music to open new paths.
[*] A poetic and surprising realm where music is at the center of all: it is used as a source of life to empower the inhabitants, activate elements, but also as a means to communicate and express feelings.
[*] A linear story to unveil, about the quest of our violinist Philemon and the mysterious Bandmaster, who’s looking to gather musicians and reunite the orchestra before the realm definitely falls into silence.
[*] An orchestral OST, composed in house and inspired by the romantic period of classical music, entirely recorded with the Scoring Orchestra of Paris for the delight of your ears.
[*] Colorful secondary characters to meet along the way, with strong narrative beats in the form of musical cutscenes and concerts, without them speaking a single word.
[*] Different kinds of collectibles and secrets to collect in order to learn more about this realm, and improve your violinist skills! 
[*] Full support for keyboard, mouse, and controller, with different control schemes to choose from or customize. Controller usage is recommended.
[*] Accessibility features to play the game the way you like, especially useful if you’re here for the atmosphere and narration more than the challenge ! Also, full support for 9 different languages.
[*] New game modes, and other fun gameplay variants to unlock in order to take the game to its limits!
[*] Gameplay time is around 4 to 6 hours for a first playthrough, up to 12 hours and more if you’re looking to complete everything.[/list]

That's it! That's [b]Symphonia[/b]. Should we be lucky enough that you deem our humble platformer worthy of your hard-earned money, we really really hope you enjoy playing it as much as we've enjoyed making it for you.

With love,
Sunny Peak 🌄

notes.title: 🎻 Behind the Symphony #3: Music meets Machinery in the World of Symphonia
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44506357/c1f54cbca5e0a47c295225a7461f713e63f1b108.jpg[/img]

Musical greetings, dear friends! 

Today’s making-of is all about the art direction of Symphonia, how the core elements of the scenery were chosen and intertwined to become one. Ready? Let’s dive in!

As mentioned before in another making-of article, the first bit of the world of Symphonia that was thought of was the violinist, Philemon. Then we decided to create a whole musical world as a setting for our virtuoso’s journey. From there, we formed a link between musical elements, and machinery elements, that would be one of the founding stones of our art direction. But why is machinery important? Well, because the realm is mostly inhabited by automatons!

You see, Symphonia is a vast realm where music is a source of life and prosperity for the automatons and the world itself. For this reason, the production of music has partially been automatized by the inhabitants, by mixing gigantic musical instruments with colossal cogs, wheels, and other mechanisms. Thus, music and machinery are tightly intertwined, and we always considered Symphonia as some kind of a giant music box, where the world is influenced by both musical forces, and mechanical forces.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44506357/06b93afdf05bb841b575cfb4c1f6cee018d1ed21.jpg[/img]

At the beginning of the game and of the demo, you start off in the Slumbering Streets, a desolate corner of Symphonia where silence has taken over, and all that is left to hear is the heavy cranking of giant cogs. For this area, we really wanted the machinery elements to play a central role, as music itself is brought back by the rebirth of Philemon in the opening sequence. To do so, we mixed giant mechanisms, like the door, and towers rising with the theme of opera halls and orchestra rooms: red curtains, concert hall seats, and the public, composed of sleeping automatons, lacking the music needed to survive in this area. To that, we added urban elements like the train station, bells and directional signs, which allowed us to convey how this place was once a place full of life, a point of passage for the inhabitants of Symphonia.

Further in the game, you then travel in areas where music is still persistent, and this mostly thanks to the other musicians still living in this realm. This is the case in the Woodwinds Glasshouse for instance, where musical elements from the Woodwinds instruments have shaped the area, intertwined with glass and the lush foliage which took over recently. Here we can see how the music played by the musician living in the glasshouse really shaped the area. And this is a general idea we tried to follow all along: we really wanted the scenery to tell a story about how the inhabitants, the structures they built, and the music - or its absence, have tightly bonded and influenced each other.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44506357/c385e084e4db2987cf39259faf0ce83706b4565f.jpg[/img]

As you might understand, Symphonia will remain a realm shaped by the inhabitants via the use of machinery and music, but it is just as true to say that the inhabitants need music and the machinery to keep living there. This interdependence is what makes Symphonia a place of wonders … but also quite similar to how us humans are tightly connected to nature, wouldn’t you say?

I’ll leave these philosophical questions up to your reasoning! The game's release is now only a couple weeks away, and we still have much to do to prepare for launch. Until then, take care, and see you soon for the next update ! 

Sunny Peak 🌄

notes.title: 🎻 Behind the Symphony #2: The Music of Symphonia
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44506357/5a7c12e03412b89b1ffb6574ad1331b66c0a5d6c.jpg[/img]

Musical greetings, dear friends!

For today’s making-of, let’s talk about the music of [b]Symphonia[/b], and how pivotal it came to be. As you can imagine, making a game about symphonic music opened a lot of doors creatively speaking, but it also created heavy constraints.

Our first important constraint was, to be using the instruments of the symphonic orchestra throughout the OST of the game. Our composers Olivier and Alexandre opted for a style inspired by the romantic period of classical music, which was a perfect orientation to use the symphonic instruments. Together, they learnt how to compose by using those instruments, as they had no previous experience in writing classical tunes. Working on the romantic period of classical music also helped us to convey a lot of emotion and narration into our score, as it is one of the highlights of this period’s tunes (think Saint-Saens’ “Danse Macabre”, as an example!).

We also decided that some areas in the game would be heavily revolving around some instruments rather than others, which is an idea that affected both gameplay, art and music. As an example, the Woodwinds glasshouse, partially playable in the demo, is linked to the Woodwinds instruments of the orchestra, like the flutes, piccolo, bassoon…That is why we use wind as a gameplay element in this area, and why those instruments are predominant in this area’s tracks.

This logic has been followed throughout the game, with some notable exceptions! We also have evolutive tunes that come back in different variations the more you progress in the game and gather musicians, for instance. A good rule of thumb was to always use the correct instruments related to the place linked to the music, and taking into account the narrative progression in the game up to this point.

https://youtu.be/au2MRozRUGM

Our second important constraint was to compose tunes that would be recorded in real life, played by real musicians in a real orchestra! This meant composing music that would be actually playable by human hands (and mouths), but also taking into account the extra time and work for creating music sheets, booking the musicians, mixing the audio and all sorts of tasks related to a music recording. This is a lot for a first game as a studio!

We decided to contact Scoring Productions, a French company specialized in music recording, to act as our executive producer for our recording project. This new collaboration meant that we could mostly focus on the composition and creative aspect of the recording, while Scoring Productions took care of all the logistic, technical and administrative aspects of the recording. Together, we made sure that both the composition and its recording respected all our constraints and were up to par with the quality standard we hoped for [b]Symphonia[/b].

So, these were two of the main aspects of what working on the music of [b]Symphonia[/b] was like. But as you can see, there are many layers when working on the music in a game like [b]Symphonia[/b], and many people to thank for making that adventure possible. We truly hope our hard work and sincerity can be heard in the OST, and that you will enjoy your time in the symphonic realm! 

Release is only a few weeks away now… Until then take care, and see you soon for the next update!
Sunny Peak

notes.title: 🎻 Behind the Symphony #1: From Student Project to Video Game
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44506357/cf98c03985a1dc07842d3fccb385c1b3ca97e44c.jpg[/img]

Musical greetings, dear friends!

In the coming weeks we want to tell you more about [b]Symphonia[/b] and its backgrounds, and we will do this with the making-of series “[i]Behind the Symphony[/i]” here on Steam. And for today's first making-of, let's dive deeper in the conception of [b]Symphonia[/b]. As you might already know, Symphonia started off as a simple student game before becoming a more ambitious project.
 
Everything started in 2019, in the French video game school, ISART Digital … There, 13 students in their last year of studies gathered together to work on a 2D platforming game. At the time, the only elements that we already knew about [b]Symphonia[/b] were that this would be a 2D platformer in which you wield a tool in order to bounce on the ground and catapult yourself along the walls.

With a lot of brainstorming, we decided that the tool would be a violin bow, wielded by a violinist in a musical world. It proved to be an enticing decision, as it raised intriguing questions about the context of the game: [i]What is this musical world? Why is this violinist traveling? Are there other musicians?[/i]

[h3][b]Just like that, Symphonia was born.[/b][/h3]
 
We spent the whole year developing the original student game version of [b]Symphonia[/b], finally building a complete 30 minute experience, with a beginning and an end. Our objective was to earn our diploma, but most importantly we wanted to showcase how our creativity and technical knowledge could lead to creating wonders. We wanted people to delve deep into the world of Symphonia, and we already felt that there was potential to tell further interesting stories in this wonderful universe.
 
It was then released on Itch.io in the summer of 2020, and on GOG in the summer of 2021. After that, everything went fast: we participated in many student awards ceremonies and even won some of them; e.g. "Best Student Game" at GSA BAFTA 2021, Pégases 2021, BIG Festival 2021, finalist at the Unity Awards … this recognition was very heartwarming, but it also helped us realize further that the project had potential to be more!
 
We finally decided to found our own company in 2021: [b]Sunny Peak[/b] 🌄. Together, we would embark on a new adventure and try to create a much more ambitious game as an indie game development studio. To make it happen, we are accompanied by our publisher [b]Headup[/b] 🗿, who understood our vision very early, and helped us with numerous tasks like helping with marketing, and funding our development process among other things.
 
Of course, we have many more people to thank for helping us create [b]Symphonia[/b] and for supporting us for so many years. But that will be for another making-of perhaps! Until then take care, and see you soon for the next update - this will be an exciting one. Promise! 😊
 
Talk to you again really soon!

notes.title: We are happy to announce Headup as the publishing partner for Symphonia! 🎼
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44506357/43b4de9f8fe1cee3e02e9c17dce8899e66349950.jpg[/img]

Hey again, platformers!

The whole team here at [b]Sunny Peak[/b] is excited and happy to finally lift the curtain of secrecy, by announcing the collaboration with Headup for our first game [b]Symphonia[/b]! 

In this 2D platformer set in a musical realm, embody Philemon, the mysterious violinist. Face the many dangers that await you by using your violin and its bow, in the hope of finding talents to form a new orchestra!

[previewyoutube=_WOmYtZNaTg;full][Insert trailer video][/previewyoutube]
Some of you may already have heard about [b]Symphonia[/b] quite a while ago. That's because it also exists as a student game released in 2020! That’s right, initially, [b]Symphonia[/b] started out as a graduation project, and after working all year long and releasing the game, many players were able to share their love with us. 

A few months after releasing it publicly, the team decided to gather once more and found the development studio [b]Sunny Peak[/b]. We wanted to build our first professional project together, and keep working on this musical universe we loved.

Since then, new faces and talents joined the team, to help us create a game we can all be proud of. We hope you will enjoy the game as much as we enjoyed making it. ❤️ 

Take care and see you soon for the next update!
Sunny Peak

notes.title: 🎻 Symphonia will be playable at gamescom 2023!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44506357/8d4b5d2e2602bff459829a93471fdb86e24ec96d.jpg[/img]

Musical greetings, platformers!

We are Sunny Peak, and we proudly welcome you to our very first game [b]Symphonia[/b]! ːsteamhappyː

Imagine a world, where music acts as a source of life and energy. But since the founders and their orchestra vanished the inhabitants are divided, and the world slowly falls into silence. What if there was a way to gather a new orchestra? That's the question Philemon, the mysterious musician in [b]Symphonia[/b], will have to answer.

A completely non-violent experience, [b]Symphonia[/b] integrates music into every element, from the gameplay and hand-drawn art to the mechanisms controlling the game world. With violin and bow in hand, you’ll jump, bounce, and explore a poetic world and activate the machinery of the realm to bring it back to life.

If you want to get a first glimpse of [b]Symphonia[/b] and try the game yourself, you'll get the chance at next weeks [b]gamescom in Cologne from August 23 till August 27[/b]. We will share further information like the hall and the booth number with you as soon as possible!

Talk to you soon, friends!
Sunny Peak
